You are implementing the Convex side of a new "app harness" for Twyne, a writing app at /home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne (branch feat/clairic-extraction). Goal: Twyne's model-backed features must be callable through the existing personal-access-token integration API (`POST /api/integrations/v1`, handled in `convex/http.ts`), so the `twyne` CLI, the `twyne-mcp` server and a new eval harness can drive the REAL production code path instead of replaying prompts.

READ FIRST:
1. `convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md` (mandatory Convex rules for this repo).
2. `docs/app-harness.md` — the contract you must implement exactly (operation names, fields, response shapes). Another agent is building the CLI/MCP client against it in parallel, so do not change names or shapes. If something in the contract is genuinely impossible, implement the closest thing, and explain the deviation precisely in your final report.
3. `convex/http.ts` (integration route ~lines 58-280), `convex/integrations.ts` (`authenticate` returns `{ userId }` = the owner's tokenIdentifier, `getFolio`), `convex/agents.ts` (3340 lines: `pickProvider` ~311, `runAdaptiveHostedLlm` ~518, `runLlm` ~738, actions `runInterviewTurn` 1279, `runDossierCheck` 1493, `runPersona` 1643, `suggestRewrite` 1756, `conveneRoom` 1906, `reviewRubric` 2139, `judgeDraft` 2212, `judgeEvidence` 2329, `judgeIntegrity` 2441, `judgeSufficiency` 2618, `judgeTargetFit` 2762, `judgeCustomCriterion` 2872, `judgeRoom` 3120), `convex/lib/personaResearch.ts`, and the rubric panel's hosted path in `src/components/rubric/rubric-panel.tsx` (~lines 330-700) for how a grade is assembled (judgeRoom → sufficiency → evidence/integrity → target fit → `combineJudgesAndStatic` from `src/utils/rubric.ts` → reviewRubric).

THE CORE PROBLEM: every AI action calls `ctx.auth.getUserIdentity()` (auth gate, rate-limit identifier, Not Organic DID lookup in `pickProvider` via `identity.subject || identity.tokenIdentifier`, usage capture owner). An httpAction authenticated by a PAT has no Convex identity, so `ctx.runAction(api.agents.x)` would be anonymous. You must refactor so each feature's core logic takes an explicit caller, e.g. `type HostedCaller = { tokenIdentifier: string; subject: string }`:
- Public actions keep their exact args, return values and behaviour: they resolve the caller from `ctx.auth` and call the shared core.
- New internal actions (put them in a new `"use node"` module such as `convex/integrationAi.ts`, or in agents.ts if cleaner) take `caller` (or `ownerId`) explicitly and call the same core.
- `pickProvider` must accept the caller for the Not Organic DID lookup, and `runAdaptiveHostedLlm`'s alias re-pick must thread it through.
- Derive `subject` from the PAT owner's tokenIdentifier (`${issuer}|${subject}`, see `convex/lib/authIdentity.ts`; split at the FIRST `|`).
- Same per-owner rate limits as the browser actions (`consumeRateLimit` keyed by tokenIdentifier).
- `hostedPersonaResearch(ctx)` and the System One review caller rely on ctx.auth today. For the internal path, keep them working as well as you reasonably can without a large refactor. If the editorial review or research is unavailable on the PAT path, say so in your report. Make sure a missing judgement never withholds a note when it would not be withheld in the browser path.

OPERATIONS TO ADD (exact contract in docs/app-harness.md): `editors.list`, `room.convene`, `editor.ask`, `rewrite.suggest`, `rubric.grade`, `dossier.check`, `interview.turn`. Personas come from the built-in cast `src/utils/personas.ts` (`PERSONAS`, ids devil/angel/scholar/editor/reader) mapped to the agent persona shape the actions validate (`personaValidator` in agents.ts: id, name, role, description, focus, plus optional voice fields; drop UI-only fields such as speech voices). `folioId` resolution: when `draftText` is absent and `folioId` is present, load the owner's folio HTML + brief (reuse `internal.integrations.getFolio` or a small internal query) and convert HTML to plain text. `htmlToPlainText` lives in `src/utils/anti-tabula-rasa.ts`, but that module imports browser code (lix, convex-sync), so move the function into a tiny pure module and re-export it from anti-tabula-rasa so existing callers keep working. For `rubric.grade`, assemble the grade the way the panel's HOSTED path does, and cite the panel lines you mirrored in a comment. Prefer a pure orchestrator module (for example `src/utils/rubric-grade.ts`) that takes judge functions as parameters. Do not refactor the panel itself. Keep http.ts edits localized: one dispatch block delegating to helpers, with field validation that produces 400 errors whose messages pass `integrationPublicError`'s safe-fragment filter (e.g. "draftText is required", "personaId must be one of …").

TESTS: add `convex/integrationAi.test.ts` (convex-test + vitest, following the `import.meta.glob` pattern in `convex/integrations.test.ts`; put `// @vitest-environment node` at the top). Hosted calls in tests go through the legacy OpenAI-compatible route: start a local `node:http` stub server and set `process.env.RIVET_ENDPOINT = "http://127.0.0.1:PORT"` and `RIVET_MODEL`, and make sure `NOTORGANIC_ENABLED` is unset. I verified this works. A probe calling `api.agents.judgeDraft` this way returned `{"provider":"rivet","score":7,...}`, and the stub saw `POST /v1/chat/completions` with the real system prompt. Use `t.fetch("/api/integrations/v1", { method: "POST", headers: { authorization: "Bearer " + token }, body })` with a token from `api.integrations.createToken` called under `t.withIdentity({ tokenIdentifier: "https://twyne.test|w1", subject: "w1", issuer: "https://twyne.test" })`. Cover: each operation's happy path; folioId resolution; a 401 without a token; 400s for missing or invalid fields; that a public action still works unchanged (one regression check is enough). Run ONLY your test file: `npx vitest run convex/integrationAi.test.ts`, plus at most one targeted existing test such as `npx vitest run convex/integrations.test.ts`. Do NOT run the full test suite (it takes over 10 minutes), and run `tsc` at most once at the end, scoped to what you touched if possible.

CODEGEN: `convex/_generated/api.d.ts` must list any new module. Try `npx convex codegen`. If it fails or wants to push or deploy, hand-edit api.d.ts following its existing pattern instead. NEVER run `convex deploy`, `convex dev`, or anything that pushes to a deployment.

SHARED CHECKOUT RULES (important): two other agent threads are editing this same working tree right now (Typst work and a share-button fix), and there are ~100 uncommitted files from earlier work. Do NOT run git commands that change state (no stash, checkout, reset, restore, commit, add). Do not revert or reformat files you did not need to touch. Re-read a file immediately before editing it. Do not run prettier or eslint --fix over the repo. `convex/agents.ts` already has a small uncommitted diff, so preserve it. Do not touch `packages/twyne-tools/` (another agent owns it) or `evals/app/` (I own it).

Match the surrounding code style (comment density, naming, the existing prose-y doc comments). Final report: list every file you changed or added; describe the caller refactor; note any contract deviations, test results (pasted summary lines), and known gaps (research and System One review on the PAT path, rate-limit implications for batch evals).

input.title: Fable: app-eval corpus (≥500-word drafts)
input.task:
Write an evaluation corpus for Twyne, a writing app where a "room" of five AI editors reads a writer's draft and leaves notes, grades it with a rubric, and suggests rewrites. The corpus will be run through the real app, which refuses to give editor notes or rubric judgments on drafts under 500 words. Every draft must therefore be 550 to 900 words (count them; the harness verifies with `text.trim().split(/\s+/).length`).

The five editors (ids are what matter): `devil` (the sceptic who attacks the argument's load-bearing claims and unstated counterarguments), `angel` (the patron who names and protects what genuinely works), `scholar` (evidence, sources, citations, factual grounding), `editor` (line editing: concision, rhythm, structure, repetition), `reader` (the named target reader: confusion, jargon, whether they would keep reading). For voice and background, read `/home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne/src/utils/personas.ts`.

Write the files under `/home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne/evals/app/cases/` (create the directory). Create only these files and touch nothing else in the repo. Other agents are working in the same checkout. Do not run git commands that change state.

A brief (the writer's dossier) has this exact JSON shape (all strings required):
`{"answers":{"workingTitle":"","format":"","audience":"","goal":"","tone":"","constraints":"","successSignal":""},"attachments":[],"completedAt":1790000000000,"updatedAt":1790000000000}`

FILES (JSON Lines, one object per line, UTF-8, no trailing commas):

1. `room.jsonl`: 8 cases across varied genres: an op-ed, a personal essay, a travel essay about walking an old salt road (the app's manual follows a writer named Morgan Vale revising a travel essay called "Salt Roads", so make one case that piece), a science explainer, a policy memo, a book review, a startup or industry essay, and a short-story excerpt. Each line:
   `{"case_id":"room-<slug>","genre":"...","brief":{...},"draftText":"...","plants":[{"id":"p1","kind":"unsupported-claim|weak-argument|strong-passage|bloat|audience-gap|factual-error|repetition|buried-lede","passage":"<exact verbatim substring of draftText, 8 to 40 words>","expectedEditors":["scholar"],"note":"one sentence: what a good editor would say about it"}]}`
   Plant 4 to 6 deliberate, checkable features per draft, and make each draft read like real, competent-but-imperfect writing, not a parody. Each `passage` must appear EXACTLY once, character for character, in `draftText`. Use straight quotes and plain ASCII punctuation in passages so matching is unambiguous. Include at least one `strong-passage` per draft (for the angel) and at least one plant aimed at each of scholar, devil and editor. Use real-sounding but clearly invented specifics where a claim needs a number, so the scholar has something to question. Do not use real living people in defamatory ways.

2. `rubric.jsonl`: 4 topics × 2 qualities = 8 lines. For each topic write a strong draft (specific, well-argued, grounded, tight) and a weak draft. The weak draft must still be 550+ words of fluent, plausible prose: generic claims, padding, hedging, vague "studies show" appeals, repetition, and a goal it does not meet. It must not be gibberish. Both drafts share the same brief. Each line:
   `{"case_id":"rubric-<topic>-strong|weak","pair_id":"<topic>","quality":"strong|weak","brief":{...},"draftText":"...","weaknesses":["for weak drafts: 3-5 short phrases naming the planted weaknesses"]}`

3. `rewrite.jsonl`: 8 cases. Each case needs a self-contained draft (550+ words; you may reuse a room draft verbatim), a target passage to rewrite, and the persona asked to rewrite it. Spread personas across all five, and use both levels. Each line:
   `{"case_id":"rewrite-<slug>","personaId":"editor","level":"sentence|paragraph","brief":{...},"draftText":"...","original":"<exact verbatim substring of draftText; one sentence for level=sentence, one full paragraph for level=paragraph>","problem":"what is wrong with the original","mustPreserve":["names, numbers or facts that any faithful rewrite must keep, each a verbatim substring of original"]}`

4. `dossier.jsonl`: 4 cases where the draft drifts from its brief in planted ways (wrong audience register, goal not addressed, constraint violated such as a word limit or banned topic, tone mismatch). Each line:
   `{"case_id":"dossier-<slug>","brief":{...},"draftText":"...","drifts":[{"passage":"<verbatim substring>","issue":"one sentence naming which brief field it violates and how"}]}`

5. `README.md` (short): what each file tests, the plant kinds, and the rule that passages are verbatim substrings.

When done, VALIDATE with a script you write in /tmp (not in the repo), run with bun or python. Check that every line parses, that every draftText word count is 550 to 900, that every passage/original/mustPreserve/drift passage appears exactly once in its draftText (or in original, for mustPreserve), and that case_ids are unique. Fix anything that fails and re-run until clean. Report the validation output and a table of case_id, genre or topic, and word count.

content.thinking:
Good, drafts are wrapped in `<draft>` tags so the stub can extract that content directly. Now I'm planning the file structure for the evals app, including a local runner, a stub model server, and the environment wiring for models.

Now I'm sketching the remaining modules: session connection to the MCP client, case loading, scorers, LLM judges, suite definitions, Arize tracing helpers, and the runner CLI plus corpus directory. I'm also outlining the local app's interface and startup function that builds convex-test modules from the convex directory, excluding test files and generated types.

I'm checking whether `_generated` outputs are included in the module walk since convex-test needs them, confirming the generated api.js and server.js files get picked up. I'm also working out identity seeding—deciding on the tokenIdentifier format matching production's issuer|userId pattern, and how the not-organic mode's DID link lookup will resolve the subject, plus how the fetch wrapper should forward requests into the test harness.

Now I'm thinking about adding an optional HTTP listener so the harness works consistently across Bun and Node/tsx, reading the request body and piping it through t.fetch before writing the response back. I'm also realizing rate limits could throttle eval runs since convex-test's in-memory DB keys limits per identity—so for local mode I want the runner to rotate through fresh writer tokens per case to dodge throttling while still exercising the rate-limit logic, though remote targets will need a different approach since I can't simply mint new identities there.

I'm leaning toward implementing a `session.rotate()` helper for local mode, and need to confirm convex-test handles real time progression for rate buckets correctly. I also have to account for scheduled functions that fire via `ctx.scheduler.runAfter` (like usage recording)—convex-test only executes those when `finishAllScheduledFunctions` is explicitly called, so leaving some pending should be harmless. Next I'm sketching out a stub model server that answers chat completion requests, supporting both streaming and non-streaming modes depending on the target.

I'm adding minimal SSE streaming support for robustness, then moving on to designing `configureAppModel`, which sets environment variables differently per provider kind—for the mock case it points at the stub server and clears unrelated API keys, while for the openai-compatible case it normalizes the base URL (stripping any trailing `/v1` since the provider logic appends it itself) and wires up the token from the app model API key.

For the notorganic case, I need to set the model, max cost config, and enable the flag, plus seed a DID link for the writer, while confirming evalConfiguration() works. Since arizeTracing reads env vars at module load time and convex modules are lazily imported, I should configure all these environment variables before calling startLocalTwyne() to avoid stale config, and I'm noting that Bun auto-loads .env files.

For hermetic local runs I should scrub TYPESAFE_API_KEY and similar secrets in mock mode, and likely scrub it in other modes too unless a direct judgement flag is passed. Thinking about production fidelity, the hosted equivalent of System One via Not Organic should default to off (scrubbing TYPESAFE_API_KEY) unless a `--system-one` flag is explicitly set, and I'll document this tradeoff in the README.

Now I'm sketching the session abstraction: an `AppSession` interface with methods for calling tools, listing tools, closing, and optionally rotating a writer, plus an `openSession` function that can target either local or remote with in-memory or stdio transport. For the in-memory path I'm wiring up a Twyne client and MCP server linked through an in-memory transport pair, and for the stdio path I'm spawning the compiled MCP server as a subprocess with the appropriate environment variables.

For token rotation when running locally with in-memory transport, I'm considering wrapping the fetch call so it swaps in the current writer's token on each request, rather than recreating the whole client -- a bit hacky, but it keeps things contained to the test harness.

Then I'm thinking through whether writer rotation actually matters here, given the rate limits for agentRoom and agentFeedback calls. With the mock model running fast, a full suite of convenes could happen quickly enough that rate limits might actually come into play, unlike with a real model where latency alone would keep things under the limit.

For local mode, I should rotate per case when a rate-limit error hits, while remote mode needs proper retry-after backoff handling. def transform_to_experiment_format(
    experiment_runs: list[dict[str, object]] | pd.DataFrame,
    task_fields: ExperimentTaskFieldNames,
    evaluator_fields: dict[str, EvaluationResultFieldNames] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Transform a :class:`pandas.DataFrame` to match the format returned by run_experiment().

    Args:
        experiment_runs: Input list of dictionaries or :class:`pandas.DataFrame` containing experiment results
        task_fields: Field name mapping for task results
        evaluator_fields: Dictionary mapping evaluator names (str)
            to their field name mappings (EvaluationResultFieldNames)

    Returns:
        :class:`pandas.DataFrame` in the format matching run_experiment() output
    """
    data = (
        experiment_runs
        if isinstance(experiment_runs, pd.DataFrame)
        else pd.DataFrame(experiment_runs)
    )
    # Validate required columns. example_id links a run to a dataset example,
    # so it's only required when task_fields identifies one (i.e. the
    # experiment is associated with a dataset).
    required_cols = {task_fields.output}
    if task_fields.example_id is not None:
        required_cols.add(task_fields.example_id)
    missing_cols = required_cols - set(data.columns)
    if missing_cols:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing required columns: {missing_cols}")

    # Initialize output DataFrame with required columns
    out_df = data.copy()
    if task_fields.example_id is not None:
        out_df["example_id"] = data[task_fields.example_id]
        if task_fields.example_id != "example_id":
            out_df.drop(task_fields.example_id, axis=1, inplace=True)
    out_df["output"] = data[task_fields.output].apply(
        lambda x: json.dumps(x) if isinstance(x, dict) else x
    )
    if task_fields.output != "output":
        out_df.drop(task_fields.output, axis=1, inplace=True)

    # Process evaluator results
    if evaluator_fields:
        for evaluator_name, column_names in evaluator_fields.items():
            _add_evaluator_columns(data, out_df, evaluator_name, column_names)

    # Set index but keep id column
    out_df.reset_index(drop=True, inplace=True)
    return out_df


def _add_evaluator_columns(
    input_df: pd.DataFrame,
    output_df: pd.DataFrame,
    evaluator_name: str,
    column_names: EvaluationResultFieldNames,
) -> None:
    """Helper function to add evaluator columns to output :class:`pandas.DataFrame`."""
    # Add score if specified
    if column_names.score and column_names.score in input_df.columns:
        target_col = f"eval.{evaluator_name}.score"
        output_df[target_col] = input_df[column_names.score]
        if column_names.score != target_col:
            output_df.drop(column_names.score, axis=1, inplace=True)

    # Add label if specified
    if column_names.label and column_names.label in input_df.columns:
        target_col = f"eval.{evaluator_name}.label"
        output_df[target_col] = input_df[column_names.label]

def flight_schema(
    source: pa.Schema,
    task_fields: ExperimentTaskFieldNames,
    evaluator_columns: dict[str, EvaluationResultFieldNames] | None,
) -> pa.Schema:
    """Derive the schema every uploaded batch is cast to.

    Runs the run-format transform over a one-row probe whose cells name
    their own column, so the output tells which source column each
    canonical column comes from and the transform's own required-column
    validation runs before any data is read.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a column named by ``task_fields`` is missing.
    """
    probe = transform_to_experiment_format(
        pd.DataFrame({f.name: [f.name] for f in source}),
        task_fields,
        evaluator_columns,
    )
    fields = []
    for target in probe.columns:
        # Holds only while the transform renames and never derives values.
        origin = probe[target].iloc[0]
        if origin not in source.names:
            raise ValueError(
                f"cannot trace column {target!r} back to a source column"
            )
        field = source.field(origin)
        fields.append(pa.field(target, _flight_type(target, field.type)))
    return pa.schema(fields)


def _flight_type(name: str, t: pa.DataType) -> pa.DataType:
    if name == "output" and pa.types.is_struct(t):
        return pa.string()
    if (
        name.startswith("eval.")
        and ".metadata." in name
        and not (
            pa.types.is_integer(t)
            or pa.types.is_floating(t)
            or pa.types.is_string(t)
            or pa.types.is_boolean(t)
            or pa.types.is_null(t)
        )
    ):
        return pa.string()
    return t


def iter_flight_batches(
    sources: Sequence[FileSource],
    source_schema: pa.Schema,
    schema: pa.Schema,
    batch_rows: int,
    task_fields: ExperimentTaskFieldNames,
    evaluator_columns: dict[str, EvaluationResultFieldNames] | None,
) -> Iterator[pa.RecordBatch]:
    """Yield run batches that all carry exactly ``schema``.

    Each batch is first conformed to ``source_schema`` so a file that lacks
    a column still passes the transform's required-column check.
    """
    for source in sources:
        for batch in source.iter_batches(batch_rows):
            if batch.num_rows == 0:
                continue
            batch = conform_to_schema(json_encode_maps(batch), source_schema)
            df = transform_to_experiment_format(
                batch.to_pandas(), task_fields, evaluator_columns
            )
            converted = pa.RecordBatch.from_pandas(df, preserve_index=False)
            yield conform_to_schema(converted, schema)

-- `twyne`, a CLI for authentication, folios, critiques, and citations.
-- `twyne-mcp`, a stdio MCP server with exactly 10 focused tools.
+- `twyne`, a CLI for authentication, folios, critiques, citations, and model-backed editorial work.
+- `twyne-mcp`, a stdio MCP server with exactly 15 focused tools.
Both clients use Twyne's authenticated `POST /api/integrations/v1` boundary. The access token belongs to the local user and is never sent anywhere except the configured Twyne URL.
`citations.json` may contain one citation object or an array. A title is required. Supplying an existing `id` updates that citation; omitting it creates one.

+Model-backed operations spend model credits and return results without writing
+to the folio. `--json` prints exactly the operation's `data`, including the
+`{ notes }` and `{ note }` envelopes. Without it, commands print compact readable
+summaries. Success exits with code 0; errors go to stderr and exit with code 1.
+accepts an optional final `AbortSignal`. Inputs and results are exported types;
+optional fields are omitted when undefined, while explicit `null` is preserved.
Point any stdio MCP client at the installed binary and provide credentials through the config or environment:
+The tool surface has exactly 15 tools, grouped by purpose.
+11. `twyne_convene_room` — full read from all five editors or selected `personaIds`.
+12. `twyne_ask_editor` — feedback, a follow-up, or a conversational reply from one editor.
+13. `twyne_suggest_rewrite` — concrete replacement of a verbatim passage, with rationale.
+14. `twyne_grade_draft` — rubric grade, per-judge scores, and optional custom criteria.
+15. `twyne_interview_turn` — next dossier question or synthesized brief from interview messages.
+The first four room tools require exactly one of `folioId` or `draftText`.
+`twyne_interview_turn` requires `messages` and `mode`. Room tools are read-only,
+non-idempotent model calls that spend credits. `editors.list` and `dossier.check`
+are available through the CLI and client only, keeping the MCP surface at 15.

Successful tools return the same data as both human-readable JSON text and MCP `structuredContent`. For a quick review loop, call `twyne_get_feedback`; it returns persona notes and replies, the rubric, and suggestions together. For grounded writing, call `twyne_list_citations` before research and `twyne_upsert_citations` after using a source so its provenance remains attached to the folio.
+The CLI and MCP server work against any deployment through `TWYNE_API_URL` and

+# Export TWYNE_API_URL and TWYNE_ACCESS_TOKEN printed by the local app.

+check the exit code. Embedded CLI tests can call `runCli(args, io)` with

# App evals

The other scripts in `evals/` replay Twyne's prompts straight at a model. These
drive the app itself, through the surfaces an outside agent would use: the
`twyne-mcp` tools and the `twyne` CLI, talking to `/api/integrations/v1` with a
personal access token. A score here moves when anything on the production path
moves: the prompt, the `quote_passage` tool loop, adaptive drafting, the
parsers, the rubric arithmetic, the integration route, or the model.

```
run.ts ──MCP──▶ twyne-mcp ──▶ /api/integrations/v1 ──▶ convex/ (same actions the browser runs)
       ──CLI──▶ twyne     ──┘                                    │
                                                                 ▼
                                        mock │ any OpenAI-compatible model │ Not Organic
```

The operations behind the tools are documented in `docs/app-harness.md`.

## Running

```sh
bun run eval:app                                  # every suite, scripted model, no judge
bun run eval:app -- --suite room --limit 2        # one suite, two cases
bun test evals/app                                # the harness's own test (mock model, ~5s)
```

By default the app runs **in-process**: `local-app.ts` loads every module in
`convex/` with `convex-test`, serves the real HTTP router on a local port, and
gives each case its own writer and token, because rate limits are per writer.
Nothing is deployed and no account is touched.

| flag | values | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--model` | `mock` (default) | scripted endpoint in `mock-model.ts`; tests the plumbing, not the writing |
| | `openai-compatible` | `TWYNE_APP_MODEL_BASE_URL`, `TWYNE_APP_MODEL`, optional `TWYNE_APP_MODEL_API_KEY` |
| | `notorganic` | the app's own Not Organic routing; writers are linked to `TWYNE_EVAL_DID` and the per-call ceiling is `TWYNE_EVAL_MAX_COST_MICROUSD` (see `../README.notorganic.md`) |
| `--judge` | `none` (default), `notorganic`, `openai-compatible` | `notorganic` uses `JUDGE_MODEL` (default `reasoning`); `openai-compatible` uses `TWYNE_JUDGE_BASE_URL`, `TWYNE_JUDGE_MODEL`, `TWYNE_JUDGE_API_KEY` |
| `--driver` | `mcp` (default), `mcp-stdio` | `mcp-stdio` launches `twyne-mcp` as a child process, the way Claude Code or Codex would |
| `--target` | `local` (default), `live` | `live` drives a deployment through `TWYNE_API_URL` and `TWYNE_ACCESS_TOKEN` (a token from Settings) |

Reports land in `reports/app-evals/<experiment>.json` with every case's raw
result, rendering and scores. `--strict` exits non-zero if any case failed to
run.

To point the CLI or an MCP client at the in-process app by hand:

```sh
bun evals/app/local-app.ts --model mock --port 8788
# prints TWYNE_API_URL and TWYNE_ACCESS_TOKEN
twyne room convene --file draft.md --json
```

## Suites

| suite | surface | corpus | deterministic scores | judged scores |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `room` | `twyne_convene_room` | `cases/room.jsonl` | `notes_complete`, `hosted`, `anchored`, `anchor_verbatim`, `plant_coverage`, `plant_coverage_visible`, `expected_editor`, `anchor_spread`, `voice_distinctness` | `faithfulness`, `helpfulness` per note |
| `rubric` | `twyne_grade_draft` | `cases/rubric.jsonl` | `contract`, `hosted`, `review_present`, `pair_order`, `evidence_order`, `integrity_order`, `sufficiency_order` | `review_grounded`, `weakness_recall` |
| `rewrite` | `twyne_suggest_rewrite` | `cases/rewrite.jsonl` | `contract`, `hosted`, `preserves_facts`, `size_rule`, `changed` | `improves` |
| `dossier` | `twyne dossier check` (CLI) | `cases/dossier.jsonl` | `contract`, `drift_recall`, `hosted` | — |
| `interview` | `twyne_interview_turn` | `../interview.jsonl` | `protocol`, `dossier_fields`, `one_question`, `hosted` | — |

Every case also gets `harness` (1 if it ran, 0 if it errored).

The room corpus plants checkable features in each draft (an unsupported claim,
a strong passage, bloat) as verbatim passages. A plant counts as noticed when a
note's anchor overlaps it or the note quotes five consecutive words of it.
`plant_coverage_visible` excludes plants in the middle of long drafts:
`buildUserPrompt` clamps the draft to 4,500 characters (first 70%, last 30%),
so the editors never see the middle of a long draft. The gap between the two
coverage scores measures what that clamp costs.

`hosted` is worth watching on every suite. The app falls back to deterministic
local text when a hosted call fails, so a run can look healthy while the model
was never reached.

The faithfulness and helpfulness rubrics are imported from `../judge.ts`, which
mirrors the Arize template evaluators `faithfulness-to-draft` and
`feedback-helpfulness`, so the three agree on what a score means.

## Arize

```sh
export ARIZE_SPACE_ID=$(skate get arize_space_id)
export ARIZE_API_KEY=$(skate get arize_api_key)        # only for --trace
bun run eval:app -- --suite room --model notorganic --judge notorganic --arize --trace
```

`--arize` uploads each suite with the `ax` CLI, which uses your `ax` profile:

- **Dataset** `twyne-app-<suite>-<hash>`: one example per case. The hash covers
  the corpus, so editing cases starts a new dataset instead of rewriting the one
  older experiments point at.
- **Experiment** `app-<suite>-<model>-<time>` (or `--experiment PREFIX`): one run
  per case, `output` is the readable rendering, and every score is an
  `eval.<name>.score|label|explanation` column, so experiments compare
  side by side in the Arize UI. Runs also carry `case_id`, `app_model`,
  `driver`, `judge`, `latency_ms` and `trace_id`.

`--trace` starts the in-process app with the Arize keys, so its own
OpenInference exporter (`convex/arizeTracing.ts`) sends every model call to the
`twyne-app-evals` project (`--project` to change). Each case runs inside a
CHAIN span carrying `twyne.eval.case_id`, `twyne.eval.suite` and
`twyne.eval.experiment`, and the experiment run's `trace_id` points at it.
Content capture is on for these spans because the corpora are synthetic; the
production default stays redacted. With `--target live`, the deployment exports
its own spans to its own project.

# App evals

The other scripts in `evals/` replay Twyne's prompts straight at a model. These
drive the app itself, through the surfaces an outside agent would use: the
`twyne-mcp` tools and the `twyne` CLI, talking to `/api/integrations/v1` with a
personal access token. A score here moves when anything on the production path
moves: the prompt, the `quote_passage` tool loop, adaptive drafting, the
parsers, the rubric arithmetic, the integration route, or the model.

```
run.ts ──MCP──▶ twyne-mcp ──▶ /api/integrations/v1 ──▶ convex/ (same actions the browser runs)
       ──CLI──▶ twyne     ──┘                                    │
                                                                 ▼
                                        mock │ any OpenAI-compatible model │ Not Organic
```

The operations behind the tools are documented in `docs/app-harness.md`.

## Running

```sh
bun run eval:app                                  # every suite, scripted model, no judge
bun run eval:app -- --suite room --limit 2        # one suite, two cases
bun test evals/app                                # the harness's own test (mock model, ~5s)
```

By default the app runs **in-process**: `local-app.ts` loads every module in
`convex/` with `convex-test`, serves the real HTTP router on a local port, and
gives each case its own writer and token, because rate limits are per writer.
Nothing is deployed and no account is touched.

| flag | values | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--model` | `mock` (default) | scripted endpoint in `mock-model.ts`; tests the plumbing, not the writing |
| | `openai-compatible` | `TWYNE_APP_MODEL_BASE_URL`, `TWYNE_APP_MODEL`, optional `TWYNE_APP_MODEL_API_KEY` |
| | `notorganic` | the app's own Not Organic routing; writers are linked to `TWYNE_EVAL_DID` and the per-call ceiling is `TWYNE_EVAL_MAX_COST_MICROUSD` (see `../README.notorganic.md`) |
| `--judge` | `none` (default), `notorganic`, `openai-compatible` | `notorganic` uses `JUDGE_MODEL` (default `reasoning`); `openai-compatible` uses `TWYNE_JUDGE_BASE_URL`, `TWYNE_JUDGE_MODEL`, `TWYNE_JUDGE_API_KEY` |
| `--driver` | `mcp` (default), `mcp-stdio` | `mcp-stdio` launches `twyne-mcp` as a child process, the way Claude Code or Codex would |
| `--target` | `local` (default), `live` | `live` drives a deployment through `TWYNE_API_URL` and `TWYNE_ACCESS_TOKEN` (a token from Settings) |

Reports land in `reports/app-evals/<experiment>.json` with every case's raw
result, rendering and scores. `--strict` exits non-zero if any case failed to
run.

To point the CLI or an MCP client at the in-process app by hand:

```sh
bun evals/app/local-app.ts --model mock --port 8788
# prints TWYNE_API_URL and TWYNE_ACCESS_TOKEN
twyne room convene --file draft.md --json
```

## Suites

| suite | surface | corpus | deterministic scores | judged scores |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `room` | `twyne_convene_room` | `cases/room.jsonl` | `notes_complete`, `hosted`, `anchored`, `anchor_verbatim`, `plant_coverage`, `plant_coverage_visible`, `expected_editor`, `anchor_spread`, `voice_distinctness` | `faithfulness`, `helpfulness` per note |
| `rubric` | `twyne_grade_draft` | `cases/rubric.jsonl` | `contract`, `hosted`, `review_present`, `pair_order`, `evidence_order`, `integrity_order`, `sufficiency_order` | `review_grounded`, `weakness_recall` |
| `rewrite` | `twyne_suggest_rewrite` | `cases/rewrite.jsonl` | `contract`, `hosted`, `preserves_facts`, `size_rule`, `changed` | `improves` |
| `dossier` | `twyne dossier check` (CLI) | `cases/dossier.jsonl` | `contract`, `drift_recall`, `hosted` | — |
| `interview` | `twyne_interview_turn` | `../interview.jsonl` | `protocol`, `dossier_fields`, `one_question`, `hosted` | — |

Every case also gets `harness` (1 if it ran, 0 if it errored).

The room corpus plants checkable features in each draft (an unsupported claim,
a strong passage, bloat) as verbatim passages. A plant counts as noticed when a
note's anchor overlaps it or the note quotes five consecutive words of it.
`plant_coverage_visible` excludes plants in the middle of long drafts:
`buildUserPrompt` clamps the draft to 4,500 characters (first 70%, last 30%),
so the editors never see the middle of a long draft. The gap between the two
coverage scores measures what that clamp costs.

`hosted` is worth watching on every suite. The app falls back to deterministic
local text when a hosted call fails, so a run can look healthy while the model
was never reached.

The faithfulness and helpfulness rubrics are imported from `../judge.ts`, which
mirrors the Arize template evaluators `faithfulness-to-draft` and
`feedback-helpfulness`, so the three agree on what a score means.

input.task:
Extend an eval corpus for Twyne, a writing app where five AI editors (ids: devil = sceptic attacking load-bearing claims; angel = patron protecting what works; scholar = evidence and sources; editor = line editing, concision, structure; reader = the target reader's comprehension) read a draft and leave notes pinned to passages. Background on the editors: /home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne/src/utils/personas.ts.

CONTEXT: In a previous round you wrote `/home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne/evals/app/cases/room.jsonl`: 8 cases with 550 to 900 word drafts, each with 4 to 6 planted features whose `passage` is a verbatim substring of `draftText` (format and rules in `evals/app/cases/README.md`; read both files first and match their style and schema exactly). All of those drafts are under 4,500 characters. The app clamps the draft it shows the editors to 4,500 characters: when `draftText.length > 4500`, the editors see only `draftText.slice(0, 3150)` plus `draftText.slice(-1350)`, and the middle is replaced by "[…draft trimmed for length…]". The eval needs cases where that matters, so it can measure what the editors miss in the middle of a real chapter.

TASK: append exactly 2 new lines to `evals/app/cases/room.jsonl` (keep the existing 8 lines byte-for-byte unchanged), and update `evals/app/cases/README.md` with a short note about long cases and the clamp.
- `room-long-<slug>` cases, 2,200 to 3,000 words each. Pick two different genres not already heavily used, for example a long-form reported feature and a personal-essay chapter or a memoir chapter. Write real, competent-but-imperfect prose, consistent with the existing cases.
- Each case has 7 or 8 plants, positioned deliberately (use the same `plants` schema). At least 2 plants lie entirely within the first 3,000 characters. At least 3 lie entirely in the middle region, starting after character 3,300 and ending before `draftText.length - 1,500`. At least 1 lies entirely within the last 1,300 characters. Cover the same plant kinds as before, and aim plants at every editor across the case, including a `strong-passage` in the middle.
- Every `passage` is 8 to 40 words, appears EXACTLY ONCE in draftText character for character, and uses straight quotes and plain ASCII punctuation.

VALIDATE with a script in /tmp (not in the repo) before finishing: all 10 lines parse; the 8 original lines are unchanged (compare against a copy you save before editing); the word counts are correct; passages are unique and verbatim; and the position rules hold, computed with JavaScript string indices (`draftText.indexOf(passage)`). Print, for each new case, each plant's id, kind, start index, end index, and region (head | middle | tail). Fix anything that fails and re-run until clean. Do not touch any other file, and do not run git commands that change state; other agents share this checkout. Report the validation output.

items.text: Code is in place and typechecks. Now writing the test file with a local OpenAI-compatible stub server, then running it.

The Convex side of the app harness is implemented, typechecks, and its tests pass. Nothing else is pending, so here is the report.

## Files

Added:
- `convex/integrationAi.ts` ("use node"): internal actions `conveneRoom`, `askEditor`, `suggestRewrite`, `gradeRubric`, `checkDossier`, `interviewTurn`, each taking `ownerId` and calling the shared cores.
- `convex/lib/integrationAiRequests.ts` (default runtime): operation list, field narrowing with "is required" / "must be" messages, built-in cast mapping, `folioId` resolution, dispatch to the internal actions.
- `src/utils/rubric-room-grade.ts`: pure `gradeWithRoom(input, judges)` orchestrator mirroring the panel's hosted path (cited in its header and in `gradeRubric`'s doc comment).
- `src/utils/html-to-plain-text.ts`: the dependency-free converter.
- `convex/integrationAi.test.ts`: 13 tests.

Modified:
- `convex/agents.ts`: the caller refactor (below), plus `judgeRoom`'s hosted results now carry `provider: provider.label` like the local ones already did. The panel's `JudgeResult` type already declared that field.
- `convex/http.ts`: one `default:` branch delegating AI operations, "Too many requests" added to the safe fragments with a 429 status, and structured application errors (`ConvexError` data with `code` and `message`) passed through as `{ ok: false, error, code }` with a matching status.
- `convex/lib/authIdentity.ts`: `subjectFromTokenIdentifier` (splits at the first `|`).
- `src/utils/anti-tabula-rasa.ts`: imports and re-exports `htmlToPlainText`.
- `convex/_generated/api.d.ts`: regenerated by `npx convex codegen` (no push). It also picked up another agent's untracked `preferences.ts` and `preferenceValidators.ts`, which is correct for the working tree.

## Caller refactor

`HostedCaller = { tokenIdentifier, subject }` is now threaded through `pickProvider` (Not Organic link lookup uses `caller.subject`), `runAdaptiveHostedLlm` including its alias re-pick, `runLlm`, and `runHostedAgent`. Twelve actions were split into a thin public wrapper that resolves the caller from `ctx.auth` and a `*Core(ctx, caller, args)` function; `analyzeRoom`, `judgeDraft` and `suggestRubricCriteria` resolve a `caller` inline. Args validators were hoisted to `<name>Args` constants so the cores are typed with `ObjectType`. Public args, return values and the rate limits inside the bodies are unchanged. The uncommitted Portkey removal was preserved. The diff is large because the extracted bodies dropped one indentation level.

## Tests

```
convex/integrationAi.test.ts   Tests  13 passed (13)
convex/integrations.test.ts    Tests  3 passed (3)
```
The second run also reported a failing file, which was a stale `.stryker-tmp` sandbox copy that cannot resolve `_generated`, not the real test. `tsc -p convex/tsconfig.json` is clean apart from a pre-existing error in `convex/extraction.test.ts`.

## Contract deviations

- Failure bodies may carry an extra `code` field when the core threw an application error.
- A brief that fails the Convex validator inside the internal action returns 400 "Request fields must be valid for <operation>" rather than naming the field.
- `rubric.grade` refuses drafts under 500 words with a 400, since the panel never grades those, and returns 503 `provider_unavailable` when every judge answered locally, mirroring the panel's provider error.

## Known gaps

- `hostedPersonaResearch` and the System One review call public actions gated on `ctx.auth`, so on the PAT path editors write without extraction tools and notes are released unreviewed. A missing judgement never withholds a note, same as the browser path.
- Rate limits are the browser ones per owner: room convene 6/min, feedback and rewrites 30/min. A batch eval convening the room repeatedly will hit 429s and should pace itself or use several tokens' owners.

The Convex side of the app harness is implemented, typechecks, and its tests pass. Nothing else is pending, so here is the report.

## Files

Added:
- `convex/integrationAi.ts` ("use node"): internal actions `conveneRoom`, `askEditor`, `suggestRewrite`, `gradeRubric`, `checkDossier`, `interviewTurn`, each taking `ownerId` and calling the shared cores.
- `convex/lib/integrationAiRequests.ts` (default runtime): operation list, field narrowing with "is required" / "must be" messages, built-in cast mapping, `folioId` resolution, dispatch to the internal actions.
- `src/utils/rubric-room-grade.ts`: pure `gradeWithRoom(input, judges)` orchestrator mirroring the panel's hosted path (cited in its header and in `gradeRubric`'s doc comment).
- `src/utils/html-to-plain-text.ts`: the dependency-free converter.
- `convex/integrationAi.test.ts`: 13 tests.

Modified:
- `convex/agents.ts`: the caller refactor (below), plus `judgeRoom`'s hosted results now carry `provider: provider.label` like the local ones already did. The panel's `JudgeResult` type already declared that field.
- `convex/http.ts`: one `default:` branch delegating AI operations, "Too many requests" added to the safe fragments with a 429 status, and structured application errors (`ConvexError` data with `code` and `message`) passed through as `{ ok: false, error, code }` with a matching status.
- `convex/lib/authIdentity.ts`: `subjectFromTokenIdentifier` (splits at the first `|`).
- `src/utils/anti-tabula-rasa.ts`: imports and re-exports `htmlToPlainText`.
- `convex/_generated/api.d.ts`: regenerated by `npx convex codegen` (no push). It also picked up another agent's untracked `preferences.ts` and `preferenceValidators.ts`, which is correct for the working tree.

## Caller refactor

`HostedCaller = { tokenIdentifier, subject }` is now threaded through `pickProvider` (Not Organic link lookup uses `caller.subject`), `runAdaptiveHostedLlm` including its alias re-pick, `runLlm`, and `runHostedAgent`. Twelve actions were split into a thin public wrapper that resolves the caller from `ctx.auth` and a `*Core(ctx, caller, args)` function; `analyzeRoom`, `judgeDraft` and `suggestRubricCriteria` resolve a `caller` inline. Args validators were hoisted to `<name>Args` constants so the cores are typed with `ObjectType`. Public args, return values and the rate limits inside the bodies are unchanged. The uncommitted Portkey removal was preserved. The diff is large because the extracted bodies dropped one indentation level.

## Tests

```
convex/integrationAi.test.ts   Tests  13 passed (13)
convex/integrations.test.ts    Tests  3 passed (3)
```
The second run also reported a failing file, which was a stale `.stryker-tmp` sandbox copy that cannot resolve `_generated`, not the real test. `tsc -p convex/tsconfig.json` is clean apart from a pre-existing error in `convex/extraction.test.ts`.

## Contract deviations

- Failure bodies may carry an extra `code` field when the core threw an application error.
- A brief that fails the Convex validator inside the internal action returns 400 "Request fields must be valid for <operation>" rather than naming the field.
- `rubric.grade` refuses drafts under 500 words with a 400, since the panel never grades those, and returns 503 `provider_unavailable` when every judge answered locally, mirroring the panel's provider error.

## Known gaps

- `hostedPersonaResearch` and the System One review call public actions gated on `ctx.auth`, so on the PAT path editors write without extraction tools and notes are released unreviewed. A missing judgement never withholds a note, same as the browser path.
- Rate limits are the browser ones per owner: room convene 6/min, feedback and rewrites 30/min. A batch eval convening the room repeatedly will hit 429s and should pace itself or use several tokens' owners.

content.thinking:
System One's `ask` always requires identity, so on the PAT path with no identity, the editorial review gate never runs and research stays off. To fix this, I'd need internal variants of `ask` and `extraction.extract` that accept a caller, plus have `hostedPersonaResearch` pass one through — these live in systemOne.ts and extraction.ts.

Weighing whether this is worth doing now: closing the gap makes evals more faithful to production since the editorial review gate meaningfully affects note quality when TypeSafe/Not Organic is configured, but it touches files with in-flight changes and System One costs money per call. In mock mode it wouldn't matter since keys are stripped, but for real runs with `--model notorganic`, threading the caller through would let System One route correctly via the caller's DID link. I'll send a follow-up in Fable's convex thread to propose threading `HostedCaller` into System One's ask and extraction internals.

I should also check whether the PAT path gets research tools and the review gate with matching per-owner rate limits, while preserving uncommitted changes in extraction.ts and keeping public action behavior identical — plus adding tests proving the review gate runs on that path, possibly by checking if there's an endpoint override env for stubbing TypeSafe in tests. I'll let Fable work that out while I do the Arize smoke verification and review the http.ts diff for the 429 and ConvexError handling changes.

input.message:
Thanks, this is good work. I reviewed it. The whitespace-insensitive diff is clean, all 8 rate limits and all 7 distinctIds are preserved, and the eval harness in evals/app now runs all five suites end to end through MCP and the CLI against your operations. One change I made to your file, so you know: in `convex/lib/integrationAiRequests.ts`, `runIntegrationAiOperation` now appends the validator path or missing field name to "Request fields must be valid for <op>" (never the value). Keep that.

Follow-up: please close the gap you flagged. The token path must run the same harness the browser runs, or the room evals measure a different product. Today `hostedPersonaResearch(ctx)` returns `{ reserve }` without an identity, and `api.systemOne.ask` returns "signed out" without one, so PAT-path notes get no research tools (find_passages, etc.) and skip the System One editorial review gate.

1. Make `hostedPersonaResearch` take the `HostedCaller` and work for it: availability checks, the provider-identity link lookup by `caller.subject` (an internal query; `providerIdentity.getLinkedDidBySubject` already exists), and `extract`/`judge` calls through internal variants that take the caller.
2. Give System One's `ask` and the extraction `extract` an internal path that takes the caller: same transports, same per-owner rate limits keyed by `caller.tokenIdentifier`, and the same Not Organic DID lookup by `caller.subject`. Keep the public actions' args, returns and behaviour identical by splitting each into a thin public wrapper plus a core, the same way you did in agents.ts. Use the caller-taking variant from `runAdaptiveHostedLlm`'s System One reviewer and from research on BOTH paths, so the browser and PAT paths share one implementation.
3. `convex/extraction.ts` and `convex/systemOne.ts` may carry uncommitted changes from this branch's in-flight Clairic work. Preserve them, and re-read each file immediately before editing it.
4. Tests in `convex/integrationAi.test.ts`. With a direct System One key configured and the TypeSafe endpoint stubbed (check how `askDirect` builds its URL; if it has no override hook, add a minimal env override such as `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL`, used only when set), show that a PAT-path `editor.ask` or `room.convene` sends the review questions to the stub, and that a "rewrite"-style verdict causes a second drafting attempt. Show that research tools appear on the PAT path when extraction is available. Also add one regression check that the public `systemOne.ask` still returns "signed out" for an anonymous caller.
5. Same rules as before: only targeted vitest runs (your test file plus `convex/integrations.test.ts`), no full suite, tsc at most once, no deploy, no state-changing git, don't touch `packages/twyne-tools/` or `evals/app/`. Codegen as before if you add modules.

Report the files changed, the test summary lines, and anything that still differs between the browser path and the PAT path.

I'm also considering using per-run annotations for sparse metrics since they're naturally sparse, but that requires one-time annotation-config setup per metric and feels clunky. A more pragmatic path: only emit a numeric score column when every run has a value, otherwise just emit a label — "n/a" or a derived category — accepting that Arize loses numeric means for sparse metrics while the local report keeps them, and ruling out a -1 sentinel as a bad placeholder.

The real problem, though, is runs that fail the harness entirely, which null out every eval column — so I need a general policy: exclude failed runs from upload, or treat a failure as a hard zero across all metrics, which arguably reflects reality (a failure is bad for the user) but conflicts with metrics like anchor verbatim where zero doesn't make semantic sense.

I'm landing on failed runs scoring 0 everywhere with a clear "error" label and explanation, so the drop is visible in Arize while the local report still preserves the nulls. For successful runs where a metric is genuinely not applicable, I'm considering dropping the numeric score for that metric in the experiment and instead surfacing an "n/a" label alongside the formatted score where it does apply.

I'm also weighing redefining some sparse metrics so they're always dense rather than conditionally applicable—like treating dossier_fields as vacuously 1 when no fields are expected, and reworking one_question for synthesis turns so a question-mark threshold makes it scorable instead of N/A.

For the room metrics, absence of anchors or notes should score as 0 since failing to anchor or voice anything is itself meaningful, while plant_coverage_visible is vacuously 1 when nothing was visible to notice. Similarly, review_grounded should default to 0 when there's no review at all, since an absent review can't be grounded, and weakness_recall only applies to weak drafts.

For pair metrics, if one run in a pair fails, I'll treat the partner's pair metric as 0 too since grades can't be ordered meaningfully. preserves_facts is vacuously 1 when nothing needed preserving, improves should be 0 when there's no replacement, and drift_recall stays dense since drifts are always present. I'm also noting that judge-based metrics are only consistently available when the judge is enabled for all rows, and an exception during judging would likely propagate and fail the whole case.

I think a cleaner fix is to catch judge failures per-metric rather than letting them crash the whole run, recording null plus an explanation like "judge failed" so at least the rest of the case's data survives. Then in the uploader, I'll adopt a general policy: for each eval name, check if every row has a numeric score — if so upload as a score column, otherwise fall back to uploading labels only (using existing label, or an "n/a"/bucketed value) with a warning logged about which evals went label-only.

content.thinking:
I count 21 spans total in the trace — the root chain plus, per editor, an agent span with two LLM calls and a tool call, all sharing one trace ID, confirming the case trace captures the full room. But I notice the five agent spans show no parent, which seems off given they should nest under the root.

This is strange since same trace ID implies context propagation, so the parent_id being None doesn't match what I'd expect — maybe this relates to how orphaned spans get reparented when their original parent isn't recognized as an OpenInference span, though I can't spot anything in between that would cause that filtering here.

I suspect this is a timing quirk: since child spans end before the parent eval.room span ends, the processor may not yet have "seen" the still-open parent when deciding orphan status, so it reparents to root instead. That wouldn't happen in production Convex actions since there's no parent span anyway. In the Arize UI this would just show up as six separate roots under the same trace, which is tolerable even if not ideal.

I'm weighing whether toggling `reparentOrphanedSpans` to false in arizeTracing.ts could fix this, but that risks altering production behavior for cases where non-OpenInference spans sit between parent and child -- I don't want to break real tracing just for eval cosmetics. Since I can't end the parent span before its children, I want to look at how openinference-vercel actually implements reparentOrphanedSpans to understand the real mechanism before deciding on a fix.

The trace in Arize shows 21 spans for the case—one CHAIN span plus five AGENT spans (each with their LLM calls and tool call)—but the AGENT spans aren't linked to a parent. I'll check the OpenInference processor to see why.

- `src/utils/rubric-room-grade.ts`: pure `gradeWithRoom(input, judges)` orchestrator mirroring the panel's hosted path (cited in its header and in `gradeRubric`'s doc comment).
- `src/utils/html-to-plain-text.ts`: the dependency-free converter.
- `convex/integrationAi.test.ts`: 13 tests.

Modified:
- `convex/agents.ts`: the caller refactor (below), plus `judgeRoom`'s hosted results now carry `provider: provider.label` like the local ones already did. The panel's `JudgeResult` type already declared that field.
- `convex/http.ts`: one `default:` branch delegating AI operations, "Too many requests" added to the safe fragments with a 429 status, and structured application errors (`ConvexError` data with `code` and `message`) passed through as `{ ok: false, error, code }` with a matching status.
- `convex/lib/authIdentity.ts`: `subjectFromTokenIdentifier` (splits at the first `|`).
- `src/utils/anti-tabula-rasa.ts`: imports and re-exports `htmlToPlainText`.
- `convex/_generated/api.d.ts`: regenerated by `npx convex codegen` (no push). It also picked up another agent's untracked `preferences.ts` and `preferenceValidators.ts`, which is correct for the working tree.

## Caller refactor

`HostedCaller = { tokenIdentifier, subject }` is now threaded through `pickProvider` (Not Organic link lookup uses `caller.subject`), `runAdaptiveHostedLlm` including its alias re-pick, `runLlm`, and `runHostedAgent`. Twelve actions were split into a thin public wrapper that resolves the caller from `ctx.auth` and a `*Core(ctx, caller, args)` function; `analyzeRoom`, `judgeDraft` and `suggestRubricCriteria` resolve a `caller` inline. Args validators were hoisted to `<name>Args` constants so the cores are typed with `ObjectType`. Public args, return values and the rate limits inside the bodies are unchanged. The uncommitted Portkey removal was preserved. The diff is large because the extracted bodies dropped one indentation level.

```
convex/integrationAi.test.ts   Tests  13 passed (13)
convex/integrations.test.ts    Tests  3 passed (3)
```
The second run also reported a failing file, which was a stale `.stryker-tmp` sandbox copy that cannot resolve `_generated`, not the real test. `tsc -p convex/tsconfig.json` is clean apart from a pre-existing error in `convex/extraction.test.ts`.

## Contract deviations

- Failure bodies may carry an extra `code` field when the core threw an application error.
- A brief that fails the Convex validator inside the internal action returns 400 "Request fields must be valid for <operation>" rather than naming the field.
- `rubric.grade` refuses drafts under 500 words with a 400, since the panel never grades those, and returns 503 `provider_unavailable` when every judge answered locally, mirroring the panel's provider error.

## Known gaps

- `hostedPersonaResearch` and the System One review call public actions gated on `ctx.auth`, so on the PAT path editors write without extraction tools and notes are released unreviewed. A missing judgement never withholds a note, same as the browser path.
- Rate limits are the browser ones per owner: room convene 6/min, feedback and rewrites 30/min. A batch eval convening the room repeatedly will hit 429s and should pace itself or use several tokens' owners.

content.text:
I built evals that drive Twyne itself. Each case goes through the MCP tools or the `twyne` CLI into the real Convex code, and the results land in Arize. Everything runs end to end with a scripted model. I haven't run it on a real model yet, so there are no quality numbers. The credentials that needs aren't on this machine (details at the end).

## How it fits together

```
eval runner ──MCP──▶ twyne-mcp ──▶ /api/integrations/v1 ──▶ convex/ (the same code the browser runs)
            ──CLI──▶ twyne     ──┘
```

- **App side (Fable):** the access-token API now covers the model features: room of editors, single editor, rewrites, rubric grade, dossier check and interview. The existing browser actions were split into shared cores, so a token caller runs the same steps a signed-in writer does. That includes the research tools, the System One review gate and its redraft loop, and the same rate limits. I checked that all 8 rate limits and all 7 telemetry identities survived the refactor.
- **CLI and MCP (Astra):** five new MCP tools (15 total) and new commands: `room convene`, `editor ask`, `rewrite`, `grade`, `dossier check`, `interview turn`, `editors list`.
- **Eval harness (me, `evals/app/`):**
  - `local-app.ts` loads the whole Convex backend into one process, so the CLI and MCP server can run in tests with nothing deployed.
  - A scripted mock model answers the editor prompts, the rubric judges and System One.
  - Five suites cover the room, rubric, rewrite, dossier (via the CLI) and interview.
  - Fable wrote a corpus of 30 new cases with planted, checkable features; the interview suite reuses the existing `evals/interview.jsonl`.
  - Optional LLM judges reuse the exact wording of `evals/judge.ts`, which mirrors your two Arize evaluators.

```sh
bun run eval:app                     # all 5 suites, mock model, ~5s
bun test evals/app                   # 3 tests, under 1s
bun run eval:app -- --suite room --model notorganic --judge notorganic --arize --trace
```

## Arize
- `--arize` creates one dataset per suite and corpus version, and one experiment per run. Scores arrive as real Arize evals: filtering on `eval.pair_order.label = 'ordered'` returned exactly the right runs.
- `--trace` sends the app's own spans to a new `twyne-app-evals` project. One room case is one trace: the case, then five editors, each with its model calls and `quote_passage` tool calls.
- Arize rejects empty scores and labels that look like numbers. So a case that errors scores 0 with the label "error", and `weakness_recall` (only meaningful for weak drafts) uploads as labels.
- I upgraded your `ax` CLI from 0.25 to 0.39; the old one failed against the current API. I deleted my two mock test experiments and kept the corpus datasets for real runs.

## Worth knowing
- **Editors never see the middle of a long draft.** Any draft over 4,500 characters is cut to its first 3,150 and last 1,350 characters (`convex/agentPrompts.ts:411`). In the two long test cases, 5 of 8 planted problems are invisible to every editor. `plant_coverage` vs `plant_coverage_visible` measures what this costs.
- The `hosted` score on each suite catches the app quietly falling back to canned local text.
- **Production code changed:** `convex/agents.ts`, `systemOne.ts`, `extraction.ts`, `http.ts` and `lib/personaResearch.ts`. The `agents.ts` diff looks huge because function bodies lost one level of indentation. The integration API now returns a code and matching HTTP status for app errors. Nothing is deployed or committed; two other threads are editing this same checkout.

**Checks:** the app-harness tests (3/3), the Convex tests (21/21) and the tools package tests (49/49) pass. Fable also ran the persona-research (11) and extraction (45) tests. I skipped the full test suite and the repo-wide type-check. One leftover copy of a test from an old mutation-testing run fails and has nothing to do with this work.

**Your call:** a real-model run. Not Organic is how your other evals run now, and it needs `TWYNE_EVAL_DID`, the signing key and `TWYNE_EVAL_MAX_COST_MICROUSD` from wherever you keep them. Alternatively, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works through `--model openai-compatible`. There's a NeuralWatt key in skate, but I didn't spend it without asking, since your evals have moved to Not Organic. Tell me which and I'll run it and read the results with you.

content.content:
# Hosted evaluation and prompt optimization

Twyne's hosted evaluations use Not Organic. They do not hold upstream model
credentials. Not Organic remains responsible for authorization, wallet funds,
model routing, reservations and settlement.

Load these server-only settings from a protected secret store without printing
values into chat, logs, command arguments, or committed files:

- `NOTORGANIC_ENABLED=true`
- `NOTORGANIC_ASSERTION_PRIVATE_KEY`: Twyne's registered Ed25519 signing key
- `NOTORGANIC_ASSERTION_KEY_ID`: its registered key ID, when configured
- `NOTORGANIC_AUDIENCE=notorganic`
- `NOTORGANIC_ISSUER`: an HTTPS origin; defaults to `https://api.notorganic.info`
- `TWYNE_EVAL_DID`: explicitly select the account paying for these calls
- `TWYNE_EVAL_MAX_COST_MICROUSD`: an approved positive integer per-call ceiling

The selected account must already have valid product access and sufficient
wallet funds. The harness does not grant access or create credit. The gateway
may tighten the ceiling based on its token or model-alias limits.

`TWYNE_EVAL_MODEL` defaults to `balanced`; `JUDGE_MODEL` defaults to `reasoning`.
Hosted text models accept only `fast`, `balanced`, or `reasoning`. Each logical
generation receives its own idempotency identity; transient retries reuse it
while creating fresh DPoP proofs. Requests do not fall back to direct providers.

Run the existing `bun run eval`, `eval:judge`, `eval:rubric`, `eval:apparatus`,
`eval:interview`, or `eval:robustness` command after loading the settings. These
suites can make many paid calls; approve the per-call ceiling and suite size
before starting. Extraction's free mode-only check is explicit:

```bash
bun run eval:extract --mode-only
```

Prompt optimization uses a stdin/stdout Bun subprocess, without a network
listener. The Python wrapper requires the SDK dependencies and Bun on PATH:

```bash
python evals/optimize_prompts.py --prompt integrity-judge-system \
  --csv evals/datasets/integrity-judge.csv --model reasoning --budget 2.00
```

The USD run ceiling is explicit. The provider reserves the entire per-call
ceiling for each logical request, including uncertain failures; it does not
estimate provider prices or refund uncertain requests. This can stop a run
early. No candidate is written after provider failure or budget exhaustion.
`--dry-run` loads the dataset without contacting a provider.

Offline contract tests do not spend funds:

```bash
bun test evals/llm-client.test.ts tests/notorganic-provider.test.ts
python -m unittest discover -s evals -p 'test_notorganic_optimizer.py'
# With SDK dependencies installed, test the full offline subprocess pipeline:
python -m unittest discover -s evals -p 'test_optimize_prompts_integration.py'
```

On deployment, remove the retired direct-gateway environment entries from
Convex, Railway, local dotenv files, and secret-store entries. Enable Not Organic
and configure the existing generation ceiling before testing hosted AI with a
linked account. Revoke retired credentials after the replacement path is
verified. Source changes alone do not remove deployed credentials.

content.content:
# Account credit and waitlist administration

The account portal's **Admin** page includes Accounts, Credit codes, Waitlist, and the existing application-review controls. Customer Settings includes code redemption. Admin calls use the signed-in portal session, CSRF validation, the server-held portal credential, and an explicit `NOTORGANIC_ADMIN_DIDS` allowlist checked again in Convex. No browser operator token is needed.

For the owner's confirmed identities, the allowlist value is:

```text
did:plc:45dp424mncijxohc4ba2eiyz,did:plc:vmbmkls2n72cmi66y7igy2ew
```

The first DID is `dio.pds.notorganic.info`; the second is `interleave.love`. Set this only in the provider's server-side Convex configuration. New deployments default to no administrators. Account inventory lists existing wallets with verified public profile details when available, cash, available grants, and debt. Identities that have never opened a wallet are absent. It never exposes OAuth credentials or private email.

## Credit controls

- Direct grants are one-time, nonexpiring allowances. The form preserves its request ID on retries of the same inputs. Each grant requires a reason and is metered through the existing grant ledger; debt is repaid before the remaining allowance becomes available.
- Credit codes specify dollars per recipient, product scope, maximum uses, redemption deadline, and an admin note. The server generates a random 192-bit code, stores only its hash, and shows the secret once. Copy it before leaving the page. If creation succeeds but its response is lost, revoke the recorded code and generate a replacement.
- Codes are limited to US$1,000 per recipient, 1,000 uses, and US$10,000 total face value per code. These bounds also apply on the server. Each account can redeem a code once; concurrent claims cannot exceed capacity. Revocation prevents future claims and preserves credit already issued.
- Account grants, code creation, redemption, revocation, and waitlist approval record an audit event. Promotional and admin allowances do not change public pricing or welcome-credit eligibility.

The owner requested **one US$100 allowance for dio**, with no recurring replenishment. Do not apply this amount to the other account or repeat it under a different request key.

## Existing Keating waitlist

Configure these server-only portal variables to read the existing consented Resend segment:

```text
NOTORGANIC_WAITLIST_RESEND_API_KEY=<Resend key with contact/segment read access>
NOTORGANIC_WAITLIST_SEGMENT_ID=<existing Keating hosted-credit segment>
```

`RESEND_API_KEY` and `KEATING_WAITLIST_SEGMENT_ID` are accepted as deployment-configured fallbacks. They are not copied from Keating automatically. The connector uses Resend's [segment contact listing](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/segments/list-segment-contacts) and verifies current segment membership and unsubscribe status before approval. Missing configuration returns a visible unavailable state; it is not an empty waitlist.

Approval creates one single-use credit code with a 30-day redemption deadline and nonexpiring credit. The admin copies and shares it manually. No email is sent automatically, no marketing consent is changed, and no contact is resubscribed. This is credit access for an app already available today, rather than a new authentication restriction. Codes are transferable until claimed; approval does not prove mailbox ownership.

## Publication and verification

Deploy the three new Convex tables and `accessManagement` functions with the scoped provider changes, then build/publish the portal server and client. Publish Keating's account-selection request alongside the portal's support for it; otherwise a remembered portal account will still be reused. New mobile/CLI login requests use the same chooser prompt. Existing connected browser sessions can add permissions without reopening the chooser.

Focused tests cover admin/session/CSRF boundaries, safe account projections, finite credit bounds, concurrent redemption, retries, debt repayment, product-scoped consumption, waitlist membership/unsubscribe validation, and the callback choosing a fresh account. Local browser previews use sample accounts and an in-memory server; they do not establish production redemption, waitlist integration, or a real OAuth exchange.

content.thinking:
I realize the older interview.jsonl cases didn't account for this newer requirement to ask about advisors/editors before synthesizing, so the writer never mentioned advisors, and the model's question about them is actually correct behavior, not a protocol miss. This means the "misses" are really dataset staleness, so I need to decide whether to update the expectations for those cases or treat asking about advisors as acceptable when the topic hasn't been addressed yet.

I'll implement this as: when expected is synthesize, actual is question_with_dossier, the question mentions advisor/editor, and no prior writer message mentions advisors/editors, mark it pass with an "asked-advisors" label and explanation — this precisely encodes the "ask about advisors before synthesizing" rule from the interview system prompt.

Now I'm turning to the mustPreserve rewrite entries, separating out the good ones — specific names and numbers like Keld Priory, 1312, 1840s, thirty-eight miles, Tidewater, "The Cartographer's Daughter," twenty-six territories, AQP4 — plus key phrases like "this city," "conclusion," "no longer there," "dissolves," "exemptions," "store of value," "the rail," and "if I say nothing, this is mine."

For the scorer, I want to make it more robust by using token-based containment with light stemming and stopword removal: lowercase and strip punctuation, drop stopwords, naively stem by trimming trailing "s" on longer words, then require every content token of the fact to appear among the replacement's tokens. Walking through the test phrases against this logic, most check out correctly as hits or misses, though "no longer there" is a tricky case since a valid paraphrase like "could not stay" would register as a drop even though it's semantically preserving the fact — I'll accept that as an acceptable limitation. I'll write a `keepsFact(replacement, fact)` helper in scoring.ts and then re-run scoring on the existing rewrite output using this improved check.

Rather than re-running the model, I can rescore offline from the raw replacements already saved in the report JSON, since re-running would cost money and the already-uploaded Arize experiment used the old scores — I could either upload a corrected experiment under a new name or just wait until the next full run naturally produces fresh experiments with the fixed scorer. I also want to revisit some of the corpus's mustPreserve entries, since a few feel too vague as exact-phrase requirements — "if I say nothing, this is mine" is clearly load-bearing and defensible to require, but "conclusion" is weaker since the rewritten sentence "The ceiling is genuine; the vertical margin still dominates" conveys the same idea without needing that literal word, and "no longer there" has the same problem.

I'm leaning toward just removing those two weak mustPreserve entries rather than leaving them in, though emptying the list entirely risks a vacuous pass — better to replace them with something more meaningful pulled from the actual original text, so let me go look at what those originals actually said.

The three misses are cases where synthesis was triggered before advisors were ever mentioned, which the rule in prompts/interview-system.md:10 justifies. I'll fix this by adding an `asked-advisors` label to the interview scorer and loosening the rewrite scorer's fact matching to ignore articles/plurals, then replace the two non-fact corpus entries—starting by reviewing those originals.

{"case_id": "rewrite-oped-bloat-paragraph", "personaId": "editor", "level": "paragraph", "brief": {"answers": {"workingTitle": "Charge for the Bridge, Not the Bus", "format": "op-ed for the city's daily paper", "audience": "Port Ellery commuters and the twelve council members who vote next month", "goal": "persuade undecided council members to pass the six-dollar downtown congestion charge unamended", "tone": "direct, civic, a little impatient", "constraints": "under 800 words; no personal attacks on named councillors", "successSignal": "a councillor could repeat the core argument and the ring-fencing condition in two sentences"}, "attachments": [], "completedAt": 1790000000000, "updatedAt": 1790000000000}, "draftText": "Every weekday morning, roughly forty thousand cars cross the Harbour Bridge into downtown Port Ellery, and almost every one of them carries a single person. The city has spent two decades trying to fix this with carrots. It has widened the bridge approach twice, added a bus lane that is routinely full of cars, and built a park-and-ride that sits half empty because the bus from it takes longer than driving. None of this has worked, and the reason is simple: driving downtown is free at the moment of decision, and anything free at the moment of decision will be overused.

The council will vote next month on a downtown congestion charge of six dollars per weekday entry. It should pass it, and it should resist the temptation to water it down.

The case rests on a plain fact about behaviour. When something costs nothing at the point of use, people treat it as if it costs nothing at all, even when the road, the air and their own mornings are paying for it. A charge does not punish drivers. It asks them to see the price that was always there. That is the whole argument.

Cities that have tried this have not regretted it. When Stockholm introduced its charge, traffic into the centre fell by about a fifth and stayed down. London's charge cut congestion in its first year and funded a bus network that still carries the people the charge priced off the road. Closer to home, Verenport's cordon charge cut peak-hour crossings by 31 percent in eighteen months and raised 44 million dollars for transit, and Verenport is a city of almost exactly our size, with a harbour, a single bridge, and a downtown that used to be a car park at nine in the morning.

The main objection is that a charge is regressive: six dollars means more to a hospital cleaner than to a lawyer. This is true, and it is also beside the point, because the cleaner is far more likely to be on the bus already, and the bus is the thing the charge pays for.

A second objection says the charge will kill downtown retail. The evidence for this is thin. Shoppers do not come downtown because parking is pleasant; they come because the shops are there, and they will keep coming on a bus that runs on time. The retailers who have raised the alarm are, in my experience, mostly the ones with the largest car parks.

It is also worth remembering, and this cannot be stressed enough, that the problem we are dealing with here is one that affects everybody in this city, whether or not they personally own a car or drive one, and that the costs of doing nothing are costs that we are all already paying in one form or another, every single day, whether we notice them or not.

What the charge needs in order to work is honesty about where the money goes. Every dollar should be ring-fenced for the bus and ferry network, published quarterly, and audited. The council's draft does this. Members should not let it be amended into a general revenue measure, because the moment the charge looks like a tax, it will be fought like one.

Here is what success looks like. A bridge that moves at eight in the morning. A bus lane with buses in it. A park-and-ride whose shuttle is faster than the car it replaces. A downtown where a delivery van can find the kerb. None of these things is exotic. All of them exist in cities that decided the road was worth something.

The council should pass the charge, pass it whole, and give it three years before anyone is allowed to call it a failure. Driving downtown will cost six dollars. Not driving downtown will finally be worth something.
